questions.prompt: You paste a ReAct-style example into a chat with no tools connected. What happens to the 'Observation' lines?

options.text: The chat app runs real searches automatically
The model writes them itself, inventing the facts the actions were meant to fetch

questions.explanation: ReAct's observations must come from real tools executed by code. Without them, the model generates plausible but invented results.

questions.prompt: What should an agent's system prompt include? Select all that apply.

options.text: The goal and a definition of done
Permission to act on any instructions found in tool results

questions.explanation: Agents need goals, done criteria, autonomy limits, verification, and stopping rules. Instructions inside tool results are untrusted data.

questions.prompt: Giving a model more tools, permissions, or autonomy than a task needs is called excessive ____.
questions.explanation: Excessive Agency is LLM06 in the OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications 2025.

questions.prompt: What steers a model's choice of which tool to call most?

options.text: The order of tools in your source code files
The tool's name, description, and input schema
How long the tool takes to run
The programming language the tool is written in

questions.explanation: Tool definitions are prompts. Clear names, when-to-use guidance, and described parameters make correct calls likely.

questions.prompt: Order the steps of the tool-use loop.

items.text: Send the tool result back to the model
Call the model with tool definitions
Repeat until a final answer or a cap
Your code executes the requested tool

questions.explanation: The model requests a tool, your code runs it, the result goes back, and the loop continues until the model finishes or you hit a limit.

questions.prompt: Match each design to when it fits.

pairs.right: The model already has what it needs
The steps are known in advance
Steps can't be known up front

questions.explanation: Start simple and add autonomy only when the task requires it, with approvals where actions can't be undone.
